notes.usage_note: Points to what you're talking about. Written は but said 'wa' as a particle.
notes.example_japanese: 私は アメリカ人 です。
notes.source_back_text:
は

(wa — topic marker)

Topic marker

Points to what you're talking about. Written は but said 'wa' as a particle.

私は　アメリカ人　です。

📐 I [topic] → American → am.

I am American.

notes.usage_note: Marks WHO is doing the action. Used for emphasis or introducing something new.
notes.example_japanese: 神様が あなたを 愛しています。
notes.source_back_text:
が

(ga — subject marker)

Subject marker

Marks WHO is doing the action. Used for emphasis or introducing something new.

神様が　あなたを　愛しています。

📐 God [subject] → you [object] → loves.

God loves you.

notes.usage_note: Marks the thing receiving the action — what is being read, loved, or eaten.
notes.example_japanese: 聖書を 読みます。
notes.source_back_text:
を

(o — object marker)

Object marker

Marks the thing receiving the action — what is being read, loved, or eaten.

聖書を　読みます。

📐 Bible [object] → read.

I read the Bible.

notes.usage_note: Connects two nouns. The first one owns the second. 私の = my.
notes.example_japanese: 私の 名前は ジョンです。
notes.source_back_text:
の

(no — possessive)

Possessive — like 's in English

Connects two nouns. The first one owns the second. 私の = my.

私の　名前は　ジョンです。

📐 My [possessive] → name [topic] → Jon is.

My name is Jon.

notes.usage_note: Shows direction or location. Points toward where you're going or where something is.
notes.example_japanese: 教会に 来てください。
notes.source_back_text:
に

(ni — to / at / on)

To / At / On

Shows direction or location. Points toward where you're going or where something is.

教会に　来てください。

📐 Church [direction] → please come.

Please come to the church.

notes.english: Where action happens / By means of
notes.usage_note: Shows WHERE something takes place, or the tool/method used to do it.
notes.example_japanese: バスで 行きます。
notes.source_back_text:
で

(de — at / by)

Where action happens / By means of

Shows WHERE something takes place, or the tool/method used to do it.

バスで　行きます。

📐 Bus [by means of] → go.

I'll go by bus.

notes.usage_note: Connects nouns together, or means 'together with' a person.
notes.example_japanese: 友達と 教会に 行きます。
notes.example_english: I'll go to church with a friend.
notes.source_back_text:
と

(to — and / with)

And / With

Connects nouns together, or means 'together with' a person.

友達と　教会に　行きます。

📐 Friend [with] → church [to] → go.

I'll go to church with a friend.

notes.usage_note: Replaces は or が to say 'also.' Great for agreeing or including yourself.
notes.example_japanese: 私も クリスチャン です。
notes.source_back_text:
も

(mo — also / too)

Also / Too / Me too

Replaces は or が to say 'also.' Great for agreeing or including yourself.

私も　クリスチャン　です。

📐 I [also] → Christian → am.

I am also a Christian.

notes.usage_note: Add か to the END of any sentence to make it a question. No word order change needed!
notes.example_japanese: 教会に 来ますか？
notes.source_back_text:
か

(ka — question)

Question marker

Add か to the END of any sentence to make it a question. No word order change needed!

教会に　来ますか？

📐 Church [to] → come? [question]

Will you come to church?

notes.usage_note: Added to the end to seek agreement or soften a statement. Very friendly and common.
notes.example_japanese: いい天気 ですね。
notes.source_back_text:
ね

(ne — right?)

Right? / Isn't it?

いい天気　ですね。

📐 Good weather → is, right?

Nice weather, isn't it?

notes.usage_note: After a place = 'from.' You will say アメリカから every single day on this trip.

から

(kara — from)

From / Because

After a place = 'from.' You will say アメリカから every single day on this trip.

📐 America [from] → came.

I came from America.

notes.usage_note: Shows an endpoint in space or time. 駅まで = up to the station.
notes.example_japanese: 駅まで 行きたいです。
notes.example_english: I want to go to the station.
notes.source_back_text:
まで

(made — until / up to)

Until / Up to

Shows an endpoint in space or time. 駅まで = up to the station.

📐 Station [up to] → want to go.

notes.usage_note: The polite 'to be.' Ends almost every sentence. Makes you sound respectful.

I am a Christian.

notes.usage_note: Attaches to a verb to make it polite. 行きます = I go. 食べます = I eat.
notes.example_japanese: 毎日 祈ります。
notes.source_back_text:
ます

(masu — polite verb)

Attaches to a verb to make it polite. 行きます = I go. 食べます = I eat.

📐 Every day → pray.

I pray every day.

notes.usage_note: Negative version of ます. 行きません = I don't go. 食べません = I don't eat.
notes.example_japanese: 肉を 食べません。
notes.source_back_text:

(masen — polite negative)

Negative version of ます. 行きません = I don't go. 食べません = I don't eat.

📐 Meat [object] → don't eat.

I don't eat meat.

notes.usage_note: Past tense of ます. Swap ます → ました. 来ました = I came. 食べました = I ate.
notes.example_japanese: アメリカから 来ました。
notes.source_back_text:
ました

(mashita — polite past)

Did (polite past tense)

Past tense of ます. Swap ます → ました. 来ました = I came. 食べました = I ate.

アメリカから　来ました。

📐 America [from] → came.

I came from America.
